findings.mechanism: functools.lru_cache(maxsize=None) on the instance method category_totals. The cache is a single module-level (class-level) dict keyed by (self, account, month). ReportService.handle creates a new ReportBuilder per request, so every call is a miss with a fresh key. The cache never evicts and strongly references every builder, which in turn holds its store reference, its _columns buffers (with the last rendered rows) and the cached totals tuple.
findings.cause: lru_cache on a method with unbounded maxsize and a per-request self
findings.evidence: Ran load.run in 3000-request batches under tracemalloc with gc.collect between batches: traced heap 6.9 -> 13.8 -> 20.7 -> 27.5 MiB (linear). category_totals.cache_info() showed hits=0 and currsize 2400/4800/7200/9600, only summary requests, which grow in lockstep with the heap.

findings.mechanism: ReportBuilder._columns lists are appended to on each render.
findings.evidence: render() clears each column list at its start, so each builder's buffers hold at most one report's rows. The builder is only kept alive by the lru_cache above; the buffers add to that leak's per-entry size but do not grow on their own.
findings.discriminator: column.clear() at the start of render (builder.py:29-30) bounds the lists to one report; a builder used repeatedly would not grow.
